newsitem.title: UK: STERLING SLIDE ACCELERATES VS MARK AND DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: STERLING SLIDE ACCELERATES VS MARK AND DOLLAR.

text.p: Sterling tumbled against the German mark for a second day in a row and hit a 10-month low against the dollar amid growing uncertainty over the UK interest rate horizon, traders said.
"The pound seemed to have calmed after yesterday's drop and the trading was thin. (But) some U.S. funds started selling and the effect was big," one trader said.
The pound dropped from session highs of 2.9825 marks to a one month low of 2.9460 after finishing in Europe on Thursday at 2.9690/00.
Brian Martin, chief economist, FX at BZW, said: "I think we've been seeing a structural shift in long sterling."
He said cable could see a support level of $1.5433 and, below that, 1.49.
"It's all moving very fast. Will it continue at this pace? That's a hard one to answer."
David Brown, chief economist at Bear Stearns, said UK economic fundamentals would eventually kick in to buoy up the pound.
"I think we're around the bottom now and within four weeks we could have a three handle on the mark again."
